Then I'm planning the offset bookkeeping, where each rank walks its owned rows in order and advances the RNG engine using discard() to reach the correct position for the next row it owns.\n\nFor each owned row, the count of non-culled pairs (where the normal dot product doesn't exceed 0.99) determines how many draws to skip, matching exactly the culling condition used elsewhere, including the edge case where degenerate zero-norm normals yield a dot product of zero and are treated as not culled. I also note that culled pairs still execute computeKij but just return a zero result, keeping behavior consistent with the original.\n\nNow I'm thinking through memory layout — storing a dense N×N kij matrix would be 1.6GB for N=20480, so distributing storage by owned rows under the cyclic ownership scheme would split that load roughly evenly across ranks.\n\nI'm weighing cyclic versus block ownership: cyclic balances work well since culling and occlusion vary row by row, but it complicates reassembling full rows during the simulation phase, since each rank's local tau and kij rows need to be gathered in the correct global order. Precomputing and storing tau per row avoids expensive per-timestep sqrt calculations, costing just a modest memory overhead alongside kij. For the simulation loop, each rank computes its owned entries for radB at each timestep, but assembling the full row across ranks via allgather requires sorting out the ownership order — cyclic ownership makes the gathered data arrive in a scrambled per-rank block order, so I'm considering switching to block ownership to simplify this reassembly step.\n\nSince the sphere is convex, rays between interior points rarely get blocked except near their own endpoints, so the occlusion work ends up fairly uniform across triangle pairs regardless of position — meaning simple equal-row block distribution should balance load well enough, and I can compute the RNG offset for each block's start as 64 times the cumulative count before it.\n\nEach rank can compute counts for its own block cheaply and then allgather them to build the prefix sums needed for RNG offsets. The real concern is that the RNG discard cost scales with the position of each rank's starting offset, so the last rank still has to discard nearly the full sequence — this discard cost is likely the dominant bottleneck at high process counts regardless of whether I use block or cyclic distribution, so I'm trying to figure out if there's a cheaper way to cut it down.\n\nI'm weighing whether a bulk-twist RNG trick could speed up the discard step, but deciding to just measure the current approach first rather than optimize prematurely. For the actual simulation loop though, progress prints every 10 timesteps are genuinely global-accurate since all ranks sync via allgather each step.\n\nI also need to handle edge cases: when P > N some ranks own zero rows, which block distribution and allgatherv handle fine with zero counts, and when timesteps is 0 the correlation loop stays empty so maxCorr and bestT just default to 0, matching original behavior.\n\nFor radiosity computation, I'll keep radE fully replicated across ranks (same T×N layout as original) since it's cheap to compute from replicated data, and preserve the same loop structure and index logic locally per rank to guarantee bit-identical floating point sums—same summation order across j for each i, and I need to double check compiler flags/contraction settings don't introduce divergence.\n\nFor the build setup, I'm using CMake's find_package(MPI REQUIRED) and linking MPI::MPI_CXX alongside the math library, keeping the executable name as roomsim and preserving existing optimization flags. It models how sound/light\n * waves propagate between surfaces in a room by computing:\n * \n * 1. Form factors (Kij) between all pairs of triangles based on visibility and geometry\n * 2. Wave propagation using radiosity equations with time delays (Tau)\n * 3. Distance estimation via cross-correlation of radiosity values\n * \n * The implementation generates a procedural icosphere mesh to simulate a room.\n */\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <array>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <map>\n#include <memory>\n#include <random>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n","newString":" * This is a simplified implementation of room impulse response simulation using\n * radiosity-based wave propagation. It models how sound/light waves propagate\n * between surfaces in a room by computing:\n * \n * 1. Form factors (Kij) between all pairs of triangles based on visibility and geometry\n * 2. Wave propagation using radiosity equations with time delays (Tau)\n * 3. Distance estimation via cross-correlation of radiosity values\n * \n * The implementation generates a procedural icosphere mesh to simulate a room.\n *\n * Parallelization (MPI, distributed memory):\n *  - Triangles are split into contiguous row blocks, one per rank. Each rank owns\n *    the Kij and Tau rows of its triangles and computes them locally.\n *  - Form factors use the same single random stream as the sequential code. Each\n *    rank skips the generator ahead to the exact draw position of its first row,\n *    so results are bit-identical to the sequential program for any rank count.\n *  - The wave propagation is advanced one timestep at a time. Each rank computes\n *    its block of radiosity values for the timestep, followed by an allgather so\n *    every rank holds the full history needed for the delayed reads.\n *  - Only rank 0 performs console output and validation.\n */\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <array>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <limits>\n#include <map>\n#include <memory>\n#include <random>\n#include <type_traits>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// ============================================================================\n// MPI Context\n// ============================================================================\n\nstatic int g_rank = 0;\nstatic int g_size = 1;\n\n// Console output is produced by the root rank only\n#define RPRINTF(...)                 \\\n    do {                             \\\n        if (g_rank == 0) printf(__VA_ARGS__); \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Contiguous block [begin, end) of n items owned by 'rank' out of 'size' ranks\nstruct RowRange {\n    size_t begin;\n    size_t end;\n};\n\nRowRange blockRange(size_t n, int rank, int size) {\n    return {n * static_cast<size_t>(rank) / static_cast<size_t>(size),\n            n * static_cast<size_t>(rank + 1) / static_cast<size_t>(size)};\n}\n\n// Per-rank counts/displacements for an allgatherv of row blocks (width elements per row)\nvoid blockCounts(size_t n, size_t width, std::vector<int>& counts, std::vector<int>& displs) {\n    counts.resize(g_size);\n    displs.resize(g_size);\n    for (int r = 0; r < g_size; ++r) {\n        RowRange rr = blockRange(n, r, g_size);\n        counts[r] = static_cast<int>((rr.end - rr.begin) * width);\n        displs[r] = static_cast<int>(rr.begin * width);\n    }\n}\n\n// Maximum of a per-rank duration (seconds), valid on all ranks\ndouble maxAcrossRanks(double localSeconds) {\n    double result = 0.0;\n    MPI_Allreduce(&localSeconds, &result, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    return result;\n}\n"},"output":"Edit applied successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"diff":"Index: /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/roomsim_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/roomsim/roomsim.cpp\n===================================================================\n--- /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/roomsim_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/roomsim/roomsim.cpp\n+++ /home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/roomsim_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/roomsim/roomsim.cpp\n@@ -1,21 +1,33 @@\n /**\n  * Room Response Simulation Benchmark\n  * \n- * This is a simplified, purely sequential implementation of room impulse response\n- * simulation using radiosity-based wave propagation. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793038105805,"sessionID":"ses_e869d12b0ffe6v3ZXlGG7HzjPF","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"edit","callID":"toolu_01UMszHX8RphpM4J5GQimSmm","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/roomsim_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r3/roomsim/roomsim.cpp","oldString":"void runSimulation(SimulationState& state) {\n    printf(\"Running wave propagation simulation...\\n\");\n\n    for (size_t t = 0; t < state.numTimesteps; ++t) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n            val_t sumB = ZERO;\n\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < state.numTriangles; ++j) {\n                if (i == j) continue;\n\n                int tauij = state.tau[state.idx2d(i, j)];\n\n                // Skip if wave hasn't yet propagated from j to i\n                if (static_cast<int>(t) < tauij) continue;\n\n                val_t kij = state.kij[state.idx2d(i, j)];\n                if (kij <= ZERO) continue;\n\n                // Get radiosity from source triangle at time when emission occurred\n                size_t srcTime = t - static_cast<size_t>(tauij);\n                val_t radJ = state.radB[state.idxTN(srcTime, j)];\n                if (radJ <= ZERO) continue;\n\n                // Accumulate contribution: form factor * area * source radiosity\n                sumB += std::min(kij * state.areas[j], ONE) * radJ;\n            }\n\n            // Update radiosity: reflection + emission\n            state.radB[state.idxTN(t, i)] = state.rho[i] * sumB + state.radE[state.idxTN(t, i)];\n        }\n\n        if ((t + 1) % 10 == 0 || t + 1 == state.numTimesteps) {\n            printf(\"  Timestep %zu/%zu\\n\", t + 1, state.numTimesteps);\n        }\n    }\n}","newString":"void runSimulation(SimulationState& state) {\n    RPRINTF(\"Running wave propagation simulation...\\n\");\n\n    // Every tau is >= 1 (distinct triangle centers are at least 0.5 apart in time\n    // units), so timestep t only reads radiosity from earlier timesteps. All blocks\n    // of a timestep are therefore independent and can be computed concurrently.\n    const size_t n = state.numTriangles;\n    std::vector<int> counts, displs;\n    blockCounts(n, 1, counts, displs);\n\n    for (size_t t = 0; t < state.numTimesteps; ++t) {\n        val_t* radBt = state.radB.data() + state.idxTN(t, 0);\n\n        for (size_t i = state.rowBegin; i < state.rowEnd; ++i) {\n            val_t sumB = ZERO;\n\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n                if (i == j) continue;\n\n                int tauij = state.tau[state.idxLocal(i, j)];\n\n                // Skip if wave hasn't yet propagated from j to i\n                if (static_cast<int>(t) < tauij) continue;\n\n                val_t kij = state.kij[state.idxLocal(i, j)];\n                if (kij <= ZERO) continue;\n\n                // Get radiosity from source triangle at time when emission occurred\n                size_t srcTime = t -
